[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Vision Transformers (ViT) and Multimodal Models (CLIP): A Technical Guide"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction to Vision Transformers"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture applies the standard Transformer architecture directly to images with minimal modifications. Instead of processing pixels directly, ViT splits an image into a grid of non-overlapping patches, linearly embeds them, adds positional encodings, and feeds the resulting sequence of vectors into a standard Transformer encoder."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"Patch Extraction and Linear Embedding"},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"To process a 2D image with a Transformer, we reshape the image x in R^(H x W x C) into a sequence of flattened 2D patches x_p in R^(N x (P^2 * C)), where (H, W) is the resolution of the original image, C is the number of channels, (P, P) is the resolution of each image patch, and N = HW / P^2 is the resulting number of patches."},{"order":6,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class PatchEmbedding(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, img_size=224, patch_size=16, in_channels=3, embed_dim=768):
        super().__init__()
        self.img_size = img_size
        self.patch_size = patch_size
        self.n_patches = (img_size // patch_size) ** 2
        
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(
            in_channels,
            embed_dim,
            kernel_size=patch_size,
            stride=patch_size
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.proj(x)  # (B, embed_dim, H/P, W/P)
        x = x.flatten(2)  # (B, embed_dim, N)
        x = x.transpose(1, 2)  # (B, N, embed_dim)
        return x"},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Multimodal Models with CLIP"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) bridges the gap between computer vision and natural language processing. By jointly training an image encoder and a text encoder on a massive dataset of internet-scale image-text pairs using contrastive learning, CLIP learns a joint embedding space where semantically similar images and text descriptions are mapped close together."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Image Encoder: Typically a Vision Transformer (ViT) or ResNet that maps images to a shared latent space."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Text Encoder: A Transformer model that processes tokenized text sequences and maps them to the same latent space."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Contrastive Loss: Maximizes the cosine similarity of the embedding vectors of valid image-text pairs while minimizing the similarity of mismatched pairs."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing the CLIP Contrastive Loss Function"},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

def clip_loss(image_features, text_features, logit_scale):
    # Normalize features
    image_features = F.normalize(image_features, dim=-1)
    text_features = F.normalize(text_features, dim=-1)
    
    # Calculate cosine similarity
    logits = logit_scale * image_features @ text_features.t()
    
    # Symmetric loss calculation
    batch_size = image_features.shape[0]
    labels = torch.arange(batch_size, device=image_features.device)
    
    loss_i = F.cross_entropy(logits, labels)
    loss_t = F.cross_entropy(logits.t(), labels)
    
    return (loss_i + loss_t) / 2"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Vision Transformers and multimodal models like CLIP represent a fundamental paradigm shift in modern deep learning. By leveraging self-attention mechanisms across visual patches and aligning them directly with textual embeddings, these models demonstrate unprecedented zero-shot generalization capabilities across a wide array of downstream computer vision tasks."}]
